rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge, contrasted with conjecture, includes anything through which conviction and certainty can be attained.
rows.anchor: used in contrast to conjecture as well. Hence it refers to everything through which conviction and certainty can be achieved.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pairing of guidance with an illuminating Book presents the general before the specific.
rows.anchor: which clearly indicates that this is a case of mention of the general before the specific.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's guidance reached people through Prophets' oral teaching and radiant scriptures, including the Torah, Psalms, Gospels and Qur'an.
rows.anchor: through the oral teachings of the Prophets and through radiant scriptures like the Torah

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi takes guidance here to mean reasoning based on the first kind of teaching, the Prophets' oral instruction.
rows.anchor: In my opinion, the word یًدُہ refers to reasoning based on the first type of teaching.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that the opponents lack reasoning describes reality: blind adherence to inherited practice is not reasoning.
rows.anchor: this negation of a lack of reasoning is negation of reality.

rows.speaker: Idolaters
rows.claim: When called to follow God's revelation, the idolaters say they will follow only the ways inherited from their forefathers.
rows.anchor: they reply that they will follow what they found their forefathers following

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is to ask whether they would still cling to ancestral custom if Satan were leading them toward Hell through that bias.
rows.anchor: to ask them that will they still adhere to this view even if Satan is calling them to Hell

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ancestral transmission does not establish truth: the forefathers may themselves have blindly adopted their own ancestors' practices as religion.
rows.anchor: their forefathers too blindly followed as religion whatever they received from their own forefathers

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wisdom and commitment to truth require people to hear God's Book, reflect on it, and assess beliefs and deeds by its arguments.
rows.anchor: reflect on it and evaluate their beliefs and deeds in the light of the arguments it proffers.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Blind prejudice and following Satan's path can lead these people to Hell.
rows.anchor: they might end up in Hell as a result of this blind prejudice and following the ways of Satan.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nationalist appeals to religion, culture or tradition cast their promoters as guardians and can make masses reject even a great truth.
rows.anchor: Those who raise these slogans are considered as protectors of national culture and national traditions. The masses are so enamoured by their slogans

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “they are called” refers to the speakers of the reply, not to their forefathers.
rows.anchor: is not the forefathers but the speakers of these words.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'anic aslama with li denotes total submission and consignment; with ila, as here, it means humbly turning toward someone or something.
rows.anchor: In the second instance, as is the case here, it is used to humbly turn towards something or someone.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ihsan means doing something with complete perfection and sincerity.
rows.anchor: The word سانْحِإِ means to do something with utter perfection and sincerity.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The qualification muhsin defines true Islam as turning to God with devotion, perfection, sincerity and faithfulness.
rows.anchor: a person turns to God and does so with full devotion and perfection and with great sincerity and faithfulness.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hypocrites invoke God but associate partners with Him in being and rights, giving those partners and their rites real importance.
rows.anchor: would take the name of God but would associate partners with Him in both His being and rights

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addressing polytheists and blind followers, the verse says neither inherited custom nor deities will support them.
rows.anchor: revealed in response to the proponents of polytheism and of those who blindly followed their forefathers.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who sincerely and piously turn to God have grasped an unbreakable rope that specially connects them to their Lord.
rows.anchor: those who turn to God with full sincerity and piety have in fact held on to a strong rope

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The return of all matters to God warns that false supports cannot help; everyone must face Him in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: all matters will one day be presented before God. No one except Him will be the Being who everyone will have to face in the Hereafter.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse reassures the Prophet not to grieve over his opponents: they will meet God, who will present their misdeeds.
rows.anchor: This verse sounds an assurance to the Prophet (sws) and further augments the warning found in the previous verse for his enemies.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's profound knowledge encompasses everyone's words and deeds and even the secrets of each person's heart.
rows.anchor: Such is the profundity of His knowledge that He is even aware of the secrets found the heart of each person.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition ila after the verb nḍṭrr incorporates the sense of compulsion.
rows.anchor: shows that the meaning of compulsion is incorporated in the expression.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly respite lasts only a few days, after which God forces the opponents into painful punishment; the Hereafter is not remote.
rows.anchor: Here the Almighty will grant them His blessings for a few days and then force them to a painful torment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In worldly life all people are bound by nature's laws; rich and poor alike are powerless to escape them.
rows.anchor: a person is bound by the laws of nature from which he cannot escape.

rows.speaker: opponents
rows.claim: When asked who created the heavens and earth, even the opponents acknowledge that God did.
rows.anchor: they will answer that it is God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since they acknowledge God as creator of everything, Islahi says He alone deserves gratitude.
rows.anchor: if they acknowledge God to be the creator of everything, then He alone is worthy of gratitude.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is illogical to credit others who had no role in creating or governing the universe.
rows.anchor: others who neither have any role in creating this universe nor governing it?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that most do not know means their practice is unreasoned: they miss the consequences of premises they accept and deny in practice what they acknowledge.
rows.anchor: The words َونُمَلْعَی َلَا ْمُهُرَثْكَأُ ْلَب imply that what they do is not based on any reasoning.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything in the heavens and earth is God's creation and subject to Him; all depend on Him, while He alone is self-sufficient and worthy of praise.
rows.anchor: whatever is in the heavens and the earth are God’s creations and subservient to Him alone.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God alone is self-sufficient and possesses every praiseworthy attribute, no one can share His claim to gratitude.
rows.anchor: No one other than Him has the status to be regarded an associate to Him in this obligation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “words” are God's signs, which testify to His being, attributes, power and wisdom.
rows.anchor: The word ُت ٰمِلَک refers to those signs of God which bear witness to His being and attributes

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling these signs God's “words” is apt because each manifests His command kun and displays itself through existence.
rows.anchor: every sign is a manifestation of God’s command of kun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is not obscure or unknown: the abundance of His signs leaves no excuse for becoming confused and worshiping a random stone.
rows.anchor: God is not someone vague and unknown so that people get confused about Him and start worshiping whichever stone they come across.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi notes that this image had already appeared in Sūrah al-Kahf, at 18:109.
rows.anchor: What is stated in this verse, has already appeared in Sūrah Kahf in the following words:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if the earth's trees became pens and the seas, including seven more, became ink, God's signs could not all be written down.
rows.anchor: even then all of them cannot be recorded in writing.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The innumerable signs demonstrate that the creator is powerful and wise.
rows.anchor: These signs show that the creator of this universe is powerful

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's might and wisdom are basic attributes from which the Qur'an adduces monotheism, prophethood and the Hereafter; the universe's signs invite people to their implications.
rows.anchor: These three beliefs form the basic issues discussed by the Qur’ān.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The noun “ink,” parallel to “pens,” is omitted from the verse's wording.
rows.anchor: the word ادَدِمٌ parallel to ٌم َلَاۡقَا is suppressed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi calls the image in 18:109 factual rather than exaggerated: even ink made from the sea cannot record the signs within it, let alone the universe; scientific discoveries remain a drop in that vastness.
rows.anchor: what is stated is no exaggeration. It is a statement of fact.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 28 sums up the premises: the powerful, wise creator can resurrect the dead, and wisdom requires an Hereafter; otherwise worldly life would be mere amusement.
rows.anchor: Stated here is the consequence and summary of all the premises stated above.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A governing noun is omitted from the phrase about one soul; the intended sense is creating or resurrecting each soul.
rows.anchor: A governing noun is suppressed in ٍةَدِاحَّ وٍسۡفَنَ ک َّلَاِا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creating or raising one soul is no different for God from creating all humanity; one command and one trumpet blast suffice.
rows.anchor: The verse states that it is equal for the Almighty to create one soul and to create whole mankind.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing reminder of God's hearing and seeing addresses accountability: He knows everyone and can readily reckon, reward or punish them.
rows.anchor: the real purpose is to remind the addressees of their accountability

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears and sees everything, nothing escapes His knowledge, and He can readily account for, reward or punish people.
rows.anchor: nothing is beyond His knowledge and grasp. Hence, He will have no difficulty in taking account from people and in rewarding or punishing them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address shifts from plural in verse 20 to singular here; a singular address can encompass a group while emphasizing each individual.
rows.anchor: Here each and every entity of a group of people is addressed and carries more emphasis than the plural form itself.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternating night and day display God's power and wisdom, picturing their cycle as vigilant, diligent, persistent and punctual pursuit.
rows.anchor: The words also portray a picture of how vigilantly, diligently, persistently and punctually the night and day chase one another.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's power and wisdom place the sun and moon in human service, each following its ordained path punctually without deviation or delay.
rows.anchor: Both follow their ordained paths very punctually. They dare not deviate from these paths or even be late by a second

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These signs recall that the God who orders the cosmos can recreate people; no creation is His associate, and the world is not purposeless but culminates in Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: how do they imagine that the God Who has such profound signs of power will not be able to re-create them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reflection on providence rules out thinking that the system's ruler is unaware of people and their deeds; ignorance would make His nurture inexplicable.
rows.anchor: if the addressees reflect on this system of providence and power, not the slightest doubt will remain that He Who is running this whole system can be unaware of them and their deeds.
